clue.text: Cast doubt upon gospel?

blocks.note: to question something is to cast doubt upon it
Mark is one of the four Gospels

explanation.surface: Someone sceptically challenging the truth of scripture, or of anything said to be gospel truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase and the noun clue the two halves; the question mark at the end hints that the whole clue also points at the punctuation symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting that symbol after a statement turns it into a query, casting doubt on supposed gospel truth.

clue.text: Fall out from missile

blocks.note: first meaning: to have an argument and stop being friends
second meaning: a short heavy bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Fallout or debris descending after a missile strike.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to argue bitterly; as a noun it is the square-headed bolt fired by a crossbow.

clue.text: Boat corroded, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to judge a word by how it is spoken, not how it is written

blocks.note: acid that ate into metal corroded it; the past tense sounds like the number

explanation.surface: A rusty old vessel, judging by the noise it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: In rowing, an eight is a racing shell crewed by eight oarsmen plus a cox.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing crews and their racing shells are named by oar count, so an eight is a type of rowing craft.

clue.text: Child — he has to finish cloth off completely

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
to full cloth is to clean and thicken woollen fabric, a finishing process

explanation.surface: A little boy is made to complete the job of finishing a piece of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is part of the surface, attached to 'finish cloth off'. Fulling is the old textile process of pounding wool to make it denser.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to the full' means to the greatest possible extent, which is wholly or entirely.

clue.text: Exaggerate upset of vicar called in by French bishop

indicators.note: upset here means turned over, so the word for vicar is read the other way round
something called in by a person is taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, the title of a vicar
Odo, Bishop of Bayeux, the Norman half-brother of William the Conqueror

explanation.surface: A French cleric summons a disgruntled English vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Odo commissioned the Bayeux Tapestry; his name splits around the turned-round clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to carry it too far, much as exaggerating overstates beyond the truth.

clue.text: One similar to husky chap, unable to speak

blocks.note: a chap is a male
mute means without speech

explanation.surface: A hoarse-voiced fellow who has lost his voice altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like a hoarse voice, but it is the sled dog. MALEMUTE is a less common spelling of malamute, the Alaskan sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alaskan malemute is a large Arctic sled breed closely resembling the Siberian husky.

clue.text: Mr. Ackroyd murdered? I agree

blocks.note: first meaning: the victim in Agatha Christie's novel The Murder of ... Ackroyd
second meaning: radio-speak for message received and understood, hence yes

explanation.surface: A detective's suggestion that the victim was killed, met with assent.
explanation.definitionFit: Christie's famous mystery is titled after this murdered character; the same word is radio jargon for acknowledgement or assent.

clue.text: Magistrate is confused re these marks on the skin

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled up and so can be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written: the anagram fodder
taken as written: these two letters are the part left over

explanation.surface: A puzzled magistrate examines some odd marks on a defendant's skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as an equation: the jumbled magistrate is RE plus 'these marks'. Remove RE from the rearranged letters and the rest is STIGMATA.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are bodily marks or blemishes, especially wounds resembling those of the crucified Christ.

clue.text: It restricts movement around low joint

definitions.text: It restricts movement around low joint

blocks.clueFragment: It restricts movement around low joint
blocks.note: surface reading: something like a bouncer barring the way in a seedy dive
setter's reading: the joint lowest on the body, just above the foot, with a band round it

explanation.surface: A doorman controlling the comings and goings at a disreputable bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a dodgy bar; here it is the body part at the bottom of the leg, and the band worn around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring or fetter fastened round the lower leg can hobble a wearer, which limits how freely they move.

clue.text: Jargon internally used, by thieves primarily

definitions.text: Jargon internally used, by thieves primarily

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so only the inner letters of that word are kept
primarily means in the first place, so just the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters stripped off
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Insiders' slang that criminals mostly use among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: argot is the private slang of a group, originally the cant of French thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot means specialised slang, historically the secret cant spoken by criminals and the underworld.

clue.text: Provide information in French repeatedly about match

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the repeated French word goes on either side

blocks.note: en is French for in
a match gives a light
the French word for in again

explanation.surface: Briefing someone in French, over and over, about a football fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten is to inform or instruct someone, giving them knowledge they lacked.

clue.text: Bounder crazy about port

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word for crazy runs backwards

blocks.note: a bounder and a rotter are both old British words for a cad
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A cad who is wild about fortified wine, or about a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' could be the wine; it is the Dutch seaport, one of the busiest in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is the great harbour city in the Netherlands, an example of a seaport.

clue.text: Knock back drink like a king

indicators.note: knock back literally sends something backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: lager is a drink, a type of beer

explanation.surface: Downing a beer in the grand manner of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' wants to mean swallow; it signals turning the drink round.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal describes royalty, fit for or befitting a monarch on a throne.

clue.text: Labour leader, to some very right

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
some people use awful as an intensifier, as in 'awful good', meaning very

explanation.surface: The leader of the Labour Party, in some people's eyes, is extremely right-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks political after Labour, but it means legally correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful means permitted by law, so what is lawful is legitimately correct or proper.

clue.text: Marmot depicted by painter

blocks.note: first meaning: the hoary marmot of North America, named for its shrill call
second meaning: James McNeill ..., the American artist

explanation.surface: A rodent captured on canvas by an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoary marmot is nicknamed for its piercing alarm call; Whistler was the American artist famous for Whistler's Mother.

clue.text: Resolute volunteers left fighting in the street

indicators.note: in places the group of pieces inside the abbreviation for street

blocks.note: first letter of ST, the abbreviation for street
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
L is the abbreviation for left
war is fighting
second letter of ST, the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Steadfast volunteers abandoned to street warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) is the British part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart describes someone loyal, firm and unwavering, which is what resolute means.

clue.text: Sweet drink on the rocks

blocks.note: liquor is alcoholic drink
a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: A sugary cocktail served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Liquorice is a black chewy confection flavoured with the root of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice is a confection, so it counts as a sweet, the British word for a candy.

clue.text: Current down — true? False!

indicators.note: false here means not genuine, so the letters before it are not in their real order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz-style true-or-false question about whether something is presently down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present; it is the noun, a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertow is a flow of water beneath the surface running away from the shore, a kind of current.

clue.text: Journey by road in old form of transport

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
a lane is a road

explanation.surface: A road trip in a vintage vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Early aircraft with three stacked wings were flown in the First World War, now a vintage means of travel.

clue.text: Gypsy's fiddle

blocks.note: first meaning: an old name for a travelling person, originally a mender of pots
second meaning: to meddle or mess about with something

explanation.surface: A Romany musician's violin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin; it is the verb, to potter about.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller was once called by this word; as a verb it means to fiddle about trying small repairs.

clue.text: Peers seen as being a little left ip some quarters

indicators.note: this is in, misprinted; it puts the middle pieces inside the pair of compass points

blocks.note: east, one quarter of the compass
qua is Latin-derived English for in the capacity of, as being
a little of the word, just its abbreviation L
south, another quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords who are regarded in certain circles as slightly left-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' tempts as lords; here it means people of equal standing. Compass points E and S are the 'quarters'.
explanation.definitionFit: Your peers are those of the same rank or standing, which is what equals are.

clue.text: Modest, covering up always line in see-through fashion

indicators.note: something covering up another hides it inside, so one word wraps around the rest

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever
L is the abbreviation for line
shy means modest or retiring

explanation.surface: A demure person who always covers up, wearing transparent clothes all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: E'er is the poetic contraction of ever, a common crossword stand-in for always.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is diaphanous, so done sheerly means in a transparent or translucent manner.

clue.text: Collected a ship in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the abbreviation for the sea

blocks.note: taken as written
SS stands for steamship
the Med is the usual short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Someone retrieving a vessel from the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collected' looks like gathered up or fetched; here it is the adjective sense of assembled in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Massed means gathered together in a large body, just as collected means assembled.

clue.text: Like some fruit? Bananas

blocks.note: first meaning: tasting of or full of nuts, which are fruits
second meaning: slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A question about fruit answered with a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like an example of fruit answering the question; it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts are botanically fruits, so something nut-flavoured is like them; and nutty and bananas are both slang for crazy.

clue.text: Dismisses county side quickly

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket, bowls a batsman out with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet
second meaning: the short written form for the Yorkshire county cricket team

explanation.surface: A bowler swiftly getting rid of a county cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: A yorker is a cricket delivery aimed at the batsman's toes; 'quickly' signals the shortened written name of a county.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowling a batsman with a yorker gets him out, and the county team of Yorkshire is abbreviated in print.

clue.text: Differing over a tape, disappear

indicators.note: differing means turning out otherwise, so the following letters take a different form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: People arguing over a recording before it goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evaporate is used figuratively for vanishing completely, as hopes or money can disappear into thin air.

clue.text: What a doctor may get to contain one garden pest

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so the number is placed within the other letters

blocks.note: a PhD, the doctorate a doctor of philosophy earns
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A doctor's possible gain, said to contain a creature that troubles gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' in 'What a doctor' supplies the first letter, and the I goes between H and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are greenfly and blackfly, sap-sucking insects that damage plants and are hated by gardeners.

clue.text: Curses businessman who's contracted charges

blocks.note: exec is executive shortened
rates are charges or fees

explanation.surface: An angry swearing executive grumbling about his contracted fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like signed to a contract; it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil upon, which is to swear at or damn.

clue.text: Supernatural blood obtained from magic horse

indicators.note: obtained from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Mystical blood drawn from an enchanted steed.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth ichor is the ethereal fluid flowing in the veins of the gods.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth gave the gods a golden fluid instead of human gore flowing in their veins.

clue.text: When one starts to repent and washes dye out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or not in place, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A penitent begins atoning and scrubs off the colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washes ... out' wants to mean scrubbing off stains, but out signals the anagram; the ash smudge marked on foreheads gives a nice irony.
explanation.definitionFit: The first day of Lent, the Christian season of penitence, falls on this day, when believers begin repenting.
